newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Uniwear says not behind share's movement.
newsitem.headline: Uniwear says not behind share's movement.

text.p: Belgian textile holding company Uniwear said on Wednesday it was not behind unusual price movements in its share during a subscription period for one million new shares, which ended last week.

Uniwear's existing share at one stage hit 305 Belgian francs. The move upwards was noticeable because the new shares had been priced at a premium to the market price when the issue opened on March 3. The new stock was issued at 288 francs each.
The Brussels Stock Exchange has launched an inquiry into the share's movement.

Uniwear finance director Yves De Poorter told a news conference he totally denied the company or its main shareholder Connie Inc, a U.S.-registered company owned by Uniwear managing director Andrea Cattaneo Della Volta, had supported the share during the issue.
"I can assure you that neither Uniwear nor Connie have bought shares during this period," he said.

"When the share price increased over 288 francs I immediately called the Banking and Finance Commission to ask if they could give an explanation...They told us at that moment that...maybe certain people were short (covering)," he said.
Jean-Luc Amez of brokerage Smeets Verbaet, which managed the issue, said there were two possible reasons for the rise.

"It's possible that someone was playing the capital increase (by buying the existing shares) and just before delivery realised that the coupon attached was not the same and had to cover their short. Or someone was selling clients' shares at the stock price and subscribing to the capital increase on the other side, trying to take the profit himself," he said.

De Poorter said the capital increase was 40.65 percent subscribed by private investors, 9.75 percent by Connie, 27.8 percent by Belgian funds and institutions, 16.8 percent for foreign funds and institutions and five percent by foreign insurance companies.
Following the capital increase, the free float in Uniwear had risen to 50.1 percent from 29.2 percent, he said. Connie's direct stake had fallen to 19.8 percent from 24.92 percent.
